payload.source_label: The constant-coefficient linear acoustics equations have conservation form for pressure and velocity

contract.statement: For the one-dimensional acoustic system p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/ρ)p_x = 0 with constant material parameters, the source asserts that pressure and particle velocity admit a conservation-law description. Combining the state and matrix in (1.6) with the stated linear flux f(q) = Aq yields the component fluxes Ku and p/ρ, hence p_t + ∂_x(Ku) = 0 and u_t + ∂_x(p/ρ) = 0 [printed p. 2, (1.5)–(1.6); printed pp. 3–4, (1.8) and the linear-flux sentence]. The surrounding integral description expresses changes in interval totals through endpoint flux differences [printed p. 4, (1.10)]. The selected paragraph separately states that pressure and velocity are physically conserved only approximately for very small amplitude disturbances in uniform media [printed p. 4, Section 1.1.1, acoustics paragraph].
assumptions: p and u satisfy the constant-coefficient linear acoustic equations p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + (1/ρ)p_x = 0 [printed p. 2, (1.5); printed p. 4, selected acoustics sentence].
K and ρ are independent of space and time, as material constants in the selected constant-coefficient system [printed p. 2, paragraph following (1.5); printed p. 4, 'constant-coefficient'].

The differential expressions require the relevant partial derivatives; sufficient smoothness is explicitly required in the surrounding discussion when deriving differential form from integral form, without a specified function class [printed p. 1, derivative convention following (1.1); printed p. 4, Section 1.1.2].

The setting is a first-order system in one space dimension; the acoustic system models waves propagating in both directions along a one-dimensional medium [printed p. 1, introduction to (1.1); printed p. 2, introduction to (1.5)].

The selected assertion applies the preceding general observation that a constant-coefficient linear system is a conservation law with flux Aq [printed pp. 3–4, sentence spanning the page break after (1.9)].

The very small amplitude and uniform-medium qualification concerns physical conservation, as signaled by 'Physically, however'; it is not separately stated as a hypothesis needed for the algebraic flux rewriting [printed p. 4, selected paragraph].
quantifiers: Real spatial variable x and time variable t; the inherited state function has domain ℝ × ℝ [printed p. 1, (1.1), 'q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^m'].
Real-valued pressure perturbation p(x,t) and particle velocity u(x,t), forming q(x,t) = (p(x,t),u(x,t)) in ℝ² [printed p. 2, (1.5)–(1.6)].
Constant material parameters K, the bulk modulus of compressibility, and ρ, the density [printed p. 2, paragraph following (1.5)].
For the surrounding integral interpretation, any two spatial endpoints x₁ and x₂ [printed p. 4, (1.10), 'for any two points'].
